actors.title: Absentee Owner Lead List Builder — County Assessor Rolls
actors.description: Build absentee-owner lead lists from county assessor rolls: Cook County IL, Philadelphia PA, NYC. Flags out-of-state and out-of-city owners by situs-vs-mailing mismatch, LLC/trust entity owners, with class and value filters. Clean JSON/CSV leads for wholesalers, flippers, direct mail and agents.

county.description: Which assessor/parcel roll to build leads from. cook-il = Cook County IL (Chicago area, full mailing-address mismatch classification). philadelphia-pa = Philadelphia OPA (full classification). nyc = NYC PLUTO (owner names only — no mailing address in the source, so rows are corporate/LLC-owner flag lists with absentee_tier=unknown). Added 2026-10: maricopa-az, harris-tx, cuyahoga-oh, davidson-tn and dc (county rolls) and nc-statewide, ny-statewide, co-statewide, ma-statewide, ct-statewide, vt-statewide (statewide rolls; use countyName to scope nc/ny/co to one county). Every added roll publishes both an owner mailing address and a situs address; Wisconsin, Minnesota and Arkansas are deliberately not offered (their mailing state cannot be read reliably). Example: "cook-il".

absenteeTier.description: Keep only leads in one absentee tier. out_of_state = owner's mailing state differs from the property state (strongest absentee signal). out_of_city = mailing city differs, same state (out_of_county is accepted as an alias). same_area_diff_address = same city but a different street address. owner_occupied_likely = mailing matches the property. any = no tier filter. Ignored for nyc (no mailing data). Example: "out_of_state". Applied by default if omitted: "any".

entityOnly.description: Keep only parcels whose owner name looks like a legal entity (LLC, LP, LLP, LTD, TRUST, TR, CORP, INC, CO, COMPANY, PARTNERS, HOLDINGS, PROPERTIES, BANK). Great for targeting investor-owned inventory; this is the only useful filter for the nyc leg. Applied by default if omitted: false.

propertyClassPrefix.description: Filter by the source's property-class code prefix. cook-il: Cook Assessor major class, e.g. "2" = residential, "3" = multi-family, "5" = commercial/industrial. nyc: PLUTO building class, e.g. "A" = one-family, "C" = walk-up apartments. philadelphia-pa: OPA category_code, e.g. "1" = single family (applied client-side). Leave empty for all classes. Added rolls: the roll's own land-use / property-class code (e.g. Harris "A1", NY State "210", Massachusetts "101"), matched server-side as a prefix. Example: "2".

minAssessedValue.description: Keep only parcels at or above this value. Uses market_value for philadelphia-pa and assesstot for nyc. The Cook County Parcel Universe dataset carries no assessed-value column, so this filter is ignored for cook-il (a warning is logged). Added rolls: each roll's own value column (Maricopa full cash value, HCAD market value, Cuyahoga market value, Nashville appraisal, DC assessment, NC parcel value, NY full market value, Colorado appraised value, MA/CT/VT assessed or listed value).

countyName.description: Optional. For nc-statewide, ny-statewide and co-statewide: keep only one county, e.g. "Mecklenburg", "Erie", "St Lawrence" or "Denver". Checked against the counties the roll actually covers; an unknown or excluded county fails the run with the covered list (nothing billed). Ignored for the county rolls.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of lead rows to emit (caps your cost — you are billed per result row). Hard cap 10,000 per run. Example: 100.

actors.title: NYC ACRIS Deed Transfer Intel - LLC, Cash & Out-of-State Buyers
actors.description: NYC deed-transfer intel from ACRIS: each deed joined across Master, Legals & Parties into one row with BBL, price, buyer/seller names, plus LLC-buyer, out-of-state-buyer and cash-sale flags. Delta mode emits only new deeds. For agents farming just-sold, investors and title/proptech teams.

boroughs.description: Select deeds by the PROPERTY borough recorded in ACRIS Legals: 1 = Manhattan, 2 = Bronx, 3 = Brooklyn, 4 = Queens, 5 = Staten Island. Leave empty for all boroughs. Note Staten Island is thinly represented in ACRIS (206,662 of 22.7M Legals records) because Richmond County keeps its own index. Example: ["3"].

docTypes.description: ACRIS document type codes to include (e.g. DEED, DEEDO, RPTT&RET). Default DEED covers standard deed transfers. Leave empty to include all recorded document types (not recommended). Example: ["DEED"].

lookbackDays.description: How many days of recordings to include, counted back from the LATEST recorded date in the ACRIS dataset (not from today - ACRIS recordings lag by several weeks to ~2-3 months). Applied by default if omitted: 60.

mode.description: "inventory" emits every deed in the window on every run. "delta" keeps a cross-run baseline in the NAMED key-value store "acris-deed-transfer-intel-state", scoped to your borough/doc-type/window combination, and emits only documents it has not seen before. The first delta run for a given scope seeds the baseline and emits the full window; every row carries delta_baseline_status so you can tell a seeded run from an incremental one. Applied by default if omitted: "inventory".

maxResults.description: Maximum number of deed records to emit (each emitted record is one billable result). Because borough selection happens after the Legals join, the actor scans up to 20x this many recorded documents to fill a borough-filtered request. Applied by default if omitted: 100.

cashSaleToleranceDays.description: A deed is flagged cash_sale=true when no mortgage (MTGE) is recorded against the same borough-block-lot within this many days of the deed recording date. cash_sale is null (never true) when the mortgage lookup could not be completed for that parcel - see mortgage_status. Applied by default if omitted: 45.

actors.title: AD/CVD Antidumping Duty Tracker — Federal Register API
actors.description: Antidumping and countervailing (AD/CVD) duty tracker: turns US Federal Register trade-remedy notices into a structured feed. Extracts the Commerce case number, product and country and classifies each notice by lifecycle stage (initiation, determination, order, review). Keyless.

query.description: Optional keyword ANDed with the antidumping/countervailing search. NOTE: the Federal Register searches the FULL DOCUMENT TEXT, so a notice can match on a mention deep in the body -- live-measured, only 44 of the first 100 results for "steel" name steel in the title or abstract. Every row carries query_in_title_or_abstract so you can tell. Leave empty for all AD/CVD notices. Example: "steel".

sinceDate.description: Only return notices published on or after this date (maps to the Federal Register publication_date filter). MUST be YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2025-01-15 (an unpadded 2026-1-15 is accepted and padded for you). Any other format is rejected and the run fails without billing, rather than being silently reinterpreted by the Federal Register's own server-side date parser. Slash forms are rejected on purpose: live-measured 2026-08-20, an ambiguous 05/06/2026 is silently read as May 6 (US order) and returns 448 documents where the June 5 (EU) reading returns 312 - a 136-document difference on an HTTP 200, with nothing in the response indicating a format was guessed. Jan 2026 is silently read as January 1. Use for recurring monitoring windows. Empty = no lower bound. Example: "2026-01-01".

caseNumber.description: Filter to a single Commerce case number, e.g. A-570-049 (antidumping) or C-570-050 (countervailing). This is a SERVER-SIDE docket lookup across the whole Federal Register archive, not a filter over the newest page -- A-570-049 returns its 2017 Order and its 2023 Continuation. A malformed value fails the run rather than silently returning everything.

actionTypes.description: Keep only notices in these coarse AD/CVD lifecycle stages. Allowed: Initiation, Preliminary Determination, Final Determination, Order, Administrative Review, Sunset Review, Circumvention/Scope Inquiry, Rescission, Other. An unrecognised value fails the run. Empty = all stages. For the precise event (a continuation vs a new order) use actionSubtypes.

itaOnly.description: Restrict to the International Trade Administration (the Commerce sub-agency that issues AD/CVD determinations). Live-measured for 2025 onward: ITA 1,412 notices, all agencies 1,853, ITC alone 370 -- so leaving this on excludes about 24%, mostly the ITC injury side of the same cases. Set false to include them. Applied by default if omitted: true.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of AD/CVD notice records to return after merging, deduping and filtering. The Federal Register itself caps a result set at 10,000 documents; every row carries upstream_result_count and results_truncated so you can see when you hit either limit. Applied by default if omitted: 1000.

monitor.description: When scheduled, emit only notices whose document_number was not seen in a previous run -- a recurring new-notice alert. State is kept in a NAMED cross-run key-value store (the platform default store is per-run and would re-emit everything each time), scoped to this run's case number, query and agency setting. Applied by default if omitted: false.

actionSubtypes.description: Keep only notices whose precise event matches. Allowed: Continuation, Revocation, Termination, Postponement, Opportunity to Request, Scope Ruling, Amended, Correction, Panel Review, Suspension Agreement, Alignment, Extension, Initiation, Partial Rescission. Empty = all. Use Revocation or Continuation to watch for duties ending or being extended another five years.

monitorStoreName.description: Name of the cross-run key-value store used by monitor mode. Change it only to keep two schedules independent. Example: "adcvd-monitor".

actors.title: Bank Enforcement Action Tracker — OCC/FDIC/Fed API
actors.description: Bank enforcement action tracker: merges US federal bank & credit-union enforcement actions into one normalized feed. Tags each action by type (Cease & Desist, Civil Money Penalty, BSA/AML, PCA) and severity, resolves the institution to an FDIC CERT, and supports delta monitoring. Keyless.

regulators.description: Subset of federal financial regulators to include. Allowed codes: FRB (Federal Reserve, live), OCC (attempted every run; OCC's own EASearch export has been returning a 404 redirect since ~2026-07, so OCC actions are currently reported in sources_failed rather than returned), NCUA and CFPB (scaffolded, pending a verified keyless feed). Empty = all currently-enabled regulators. Requesting only unavailable regulators fails the run rather than substituting a different one. Example: ["FRB","OCC"]. Applied by default if omitted: [].

sinceDate.description: Only return enforcement actions dated on or after this day (matches the action's start/effective date). MUST be YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2024-01-15); 2024-1-15 is accepted and zero-padded. ANY other format FAILS the run before anything is fetched or billed - it is never guessed at. The value is compared against ISO action dates, so an unrejected bad format is invisible: measured on this actor's own code, 01/15/2024 returned 12 of 12 test actions labelled as a filtered answer, Jan 2024 returned 0 of 12, and 2024/01/01 returned a plausible-looking 4 of 12, against a true 6. Slash forms are rejected on purpose - 05/06/2025 is ambiguous between US (May 6) and EU (June 5) order, so guessing would trade a loud error for a silent one-month window shift. Empty = no lower bound (the whole feed). Example: "2024-01-01".

actionTypes.description: Keep only these unified action types. Allowed values: Cease & Desist, Civil Money Penalty, BSA/AML, Fair Lending, Prompt Corrective Action, Written Agreement, Removal/Prohibition, Termination, Other. Empty = all types. Example: ["Civil Money Penalty","BSA/AML"]. Applied by default if omitted: [].

institutionName.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on the institution / party name (e.g. 'wells fargo', 'century bank'). Empty = all institutions.

state.description: Filter to actions whose institution is located in this US state (2-letter code, e.g. CA, TX). Derived from the action's location / resolved FDIC record. Empty = all states.

resolveEntities.description: Best-effort match each institution name to an FDIC certificate (CERT) via the keyless FDIC BankFind API, adding fdic_cert / fdic_matched_name. Turn off to skip the extra lookups and run faster. Applied by default if omitted: true.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of enforcement-action records to return after merging, filtering, dedup, and severity sort. Example: 500. Applied by default if omitted: 1000.

monitor.description: When scheduled, emit only actions whose stable action id was not seen in previous runs - a recurring new-enforcement-action alert. State is kept in the actor's key-value store. Applied by default if omitted: false.

actors.title: BLM Mining Claims Search & Monitor API — Lode/Placer (MLRS)
actors.description: Search and monitor US federal mining claims from the official BLM MLRS national dataset. Filter by state, claim type (lode / placer / mill site) and status, and track newly recorded or modified claims. Mineral-rights and land data. Keyless, official source.

states.description: REQUIRED. Two-letter state codes to search. BLM mining claims exist in AK, AZ, CA, CO, ID, MT, NM, NV, OR, UT and WY, plus a small number elsewhere. Name the states explicitly; there is no default, so a run cannot silently answer about Nevada when you meant the whole West. Example: ["NV"].

claimType.description: Filter by claim type keyword: Lode, Placer, Mill Site, or Tunnel Site. Matched case-insensitively against BLM's inconsistently-cased product field, so it also catches the National Park variants. Empty = all types. Example: "Lode".

disposition.description: Filter by case disposition. Valid values in the Not Closed layer: Active, Filed, Submitted, Pending, Under Review, On Appeal, Appeal - Stay Granted. The value Closed exists only in the Closed layer, so it also requires includeClosed = true. BLM does not use 'Void' in either layer. An impossible value fails the run rather than returning an empty dataset. Applied by default if omitted: "".

nameContains.description: Return only claims whose name contains this text.

caseSerial.description: Look up one exact BLM case serial number (e.g. NV105216280).

sinceModified.description: Return only claims created/updated on or after this date — use for new-claim monitoring. MUST be YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-06-01) - any other format is rejected and the run fails without billing, rather than being silently reinterpreted by ArcGIS's own date parser. Slash forms are rejected on purpose: live-measured, an ambiguous 05/06/2025 is silently read as May 6 (US order) and differs from the June 5 (EU) reading by 6.0% of matching claims, with nothing in the response indicating a format was guessed. Empty = no lower bound. Example: "2026-01-01".

includeClosed.description: Also search the Closed layer (80,095 records) in addition to the Not Closed layer. Required if you filter on disposition 'Closed'. Applied by default if omitted: false.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of claim records to return per layer, most recently modified first. Every row carries layer_total_matching and result_truncated so you can tell whether you received the complete set - a statewide Nevada query matches over 275,000 claims. Example: 200. Applied by default if omitted: 1000.

monitor.description: Delta mode: emit only claims not seen in previous runs, using a named cross-run store keyed to this exact filter set. The first run after enabling it establishes the baseline and emits everything that matches. Applied by default if omitted: false.

actors.title: Sage-Grouse Habitat Siting Screener — BLM/USFS PHMA/GHMA
actors.description: Point-in-polygon screen of coordinates against seven federal Greater Sage-Grouse Habitat Management Area sources (BLM/USFS: WY, UT, NV/CA, CO, ID/MT, OR) for western wind, solar, oil and gas, and transmission siting. Returns habitat tier, managing agency, and permitting stipulation flags.

assets.description: Points to screen against seven federal Greater Sage-Grouse Habitat Management Area Record-of-Decision services (USFS Wyoming, Utah, Nevada/California, Northwest Colorado, Idaho/SW Montana; BLM Colorado and Oregon). Each item is an object with numeric lat and lon (WGS84 decimal degrees) and an optional label. One billable row per asset. Every row reports which sources answered and whether the point even falls inside a mapped sub-region. Example: [{"lat":42.985,"lon":-109.865,"label":"Pinedale Anticline, WY (Priority Habitat)"},{"lat":38.889751,"lon":-117.359478,"label":"Nevada mapped Non-Habitat (explicit absence)"},{"lat":39.7392,"lon":-104.9903,"label":"Denver CO (outside every mapped sub-region)"}].

radiusMiles.description: When a point is clear at the exact coordinate, also search this many miles around it and report nearby Greater Sage-Grouse habitat as context. v1.1 uses a TRUE circular search (the v1.0 bounding box overshot the stated radius by up to 27% at the corners) and reports an exact server-side count. Set 0 to screen only the exact point. Example: 0.

maxAssets.description: Maximum number of assets to screen from the assets list (safety cap). Extra assets beyond this are ignored. Applied by default if omitted: 25.

actors.title: BLM Solar Siting Screener — 2024 Western Solar Plan DLA Check
actors.description: Screens coordinates against the BLM Solar PEIS analysis: exclusion areas, Solar Energy Zones, DRECP focus and variance lands. Returns the specific exclusion drivers, transmission and slope screens, the plan stage the data actually represents, and a per-layer status so a clear is never a guess.

assets.description: List of sites to screen. Each item is an object with numeric lat and lon (WGS84 decimal degrees) and an optional label. One input site = one output row (one billable result). Coordinates outside BLM Western Solar Plan lands return a clean 'not within' row, not an error. Example: [{"lat":37.0168,"lon":-105.9491,"label":"Antonito Southeast SEZ (CO) - inside a Solar Energy Zone"},{"lat":36.56,"lon":-114.92,"label":"Dry Lake area (NV) - exclusion area control"},{"lat":33.6046,"lon":-114.837,"label":"Riverside County (CA) - DRECP Development Focus Area"},{"lat":33.3725,"lon":-115.7804,"label":"Imperial County (CA) - DRECP variance-process land"},{"lat":39.7392,"lon":-104.9903…(truncated).

maxAssets.description: Safety cap on how many sites to screen in one run (1–5000). Extra sites beyond the cap are ignored. Example: 500.

simulateOutage.description: Diagnostic seam for proving the failure paths without waiting for a real BLM outage. 'none' is normal operation and is what you want for real work. The corroborating option forces the row-count and Denver-negative-control probes to time out: the run must still SUCCEED, with drift_gate_status=verified_degraded on every row and the skipped probes named. The load-bearing option forces the layer-metadata and ProposedPlan-vocabulary probes to time out: the run must FAIL, emitting nothing and billing nothing. Both are routed through the same code path a genuine outage takes. Example: "none".

actors.title: BOEM Offshore Wind Lease Tracker — Inventory & Status Deltas
actors.description: Track every active BOEM offshore wind lease on the US Outer Continental Shelf: lessee, state, acreage, effective and expiration dates, plus wind planning areas. Delta mode diffs runs to flag new, removed, status- or acreage-changed leases. Keyless official data. MCP/agent-ready.

mode.description: 'inventory' emits the current unified wind-lease inventory (one row per lease, plus planning areas). 'delta' compares against the snapshot saved by the previous run in the named key-value store and emits only NEW / REMOVED / STATUS_CHANGED / ACREAGE_CHANGED rows. The first delta run seeds the snapshot and emits 0 rows. Example: "inventory".

states.description: Optional filter: only return leases/planning areas offshore of these states. Accepts postal codes (CA, RI) or full names (California). Empty = all states.

lessee.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter on the lessee/company name, e.g. 'RWE' or 'Orsted'. Planning areas have no lessee and are excluded when this filter is set.

includePlanningAreas.description: Also emit BOEM offshore wind planning-area outlines (record_type PLANNING_AREA) alongside active leases. Note: BOEM rescinded its wind planning areas on 2025-07-30; the layer is still published with an AREA_STATUS field, which this actor tracks for changes. Applied by default if omitted: true.

includeBlockCounts.description: Count the OCS blocks/sub-blocks inside each lease from BOEM's block-level layer and fill the block_count field. Adds a few extra API pages per run. Applied by default if omitted: true.

snapshotStoreName.description: Name of the Apify key-value store where the lease snapshot is persisted between runs for delta mode. Use different names to track different filtered universes independently. Applied by default if omitted: "boem-wind-lease-snapshots".

maxResults.description: Maximum number of dataset rows to emit. The full national inventory is currently ~52 leases + ~19 planning areas, so the default comfortably covers everything. Example: 500.

actors.title: US Airline On-Time & Flight Delay Statistics by Route (BTS)
actors.description: Historical US flight delay, cancellation and on-time statistics from official BTS data. Rollups by route, airline or airport and month with full delay-cause breakdowns — carrier, weather, NAS, security, late aircraft — honest denominators, cancellation causes and data-vintage on every row.

sinceMonth.description: First month of BTS on-time data to include, as YYYY-MM (e.g. "2026-05"). Leave blank to default to the month before the latest published month. The BTS series begins 1987-10 and is published with a ~2-3 month lag; the run discovers the latest available month live and reports it on every row. An unusable value (slash dates, bare years, month 13) FAILS the run loudly — it is never silently ignored. Example: "2026-05".

untilMonth.description: Last month of BTS on-time data to include, as YYYY-MM. Leave blank to default to the latest published month. A window spanning more than 12 months is rejected (each month is a ~30 MB BTS download). A month BTS has not yet published is reported as missing — with allowPartial false (the default) the run fails loudly rather than quietly narrowing your window. Example: "2026-06".

airlines.description: Optional. BTS reporting-carrier codes to include, e.g. ["WN","AA","DL","UA","B6"]. Leave empty for all reporting carriers (13 in 2026-05: AA, AS, B6, DL, F9, G4, MQ, NK, OH, OO, UA, WN, YX). A code matching no flights fails the run with the list of carriers actually present — never a silent empty dataset. Example: ["WN"].

origins.description: Optional. IATA origin airport codes, e.g. ["DEN","MDW"]. Leave empty for all origins.

dests.description: Optional. IATA destination airport codes, e.g. ["LGA","DCA"]. Leave empty for all destinations.

groupBy.description: How to roll flights up. "route" = one row per (origin-dest x month) across airlines; "airline" = one row per (carrier x month); "origin_airport" / "dest_airport" = one row per (airport x month); "airline_route" = one row per (carrier x origin-dest x month). Omitted = "route". Example: "route".

minFlights.description: Suppress groups with fewer than this many scheduled flights in a month (noise control — a 2-flight 'route' produces meaningless rates). Suppressed-group count is disclosed on every emitted row as groups_suppressed_below_min_flights. Set 0 to keep everything. Omitted = 30. Example: 30.

maxResults.description: Hard cap on emitted rows — each row is one billed result. Enforced by a single audited code path for every groupBy mode; when the cap bites, rows are dropped smallest-groups-first and every emitted row carries results_truncated=true. Omitted = 500. Example: 500.

allowPartial.description: If a requested month cannot be retrieved (not yet published by BTS, or the download failed), the run FAILS loudly by default so a partial window is never mistaken for a complete one. Set true to proceed with the months that did arrive — every row then reports months_missing and data_complete=false. Applied by default if omitted: false.

actors.title: US Airline Fare & Route-Market Analytics (BTS DB1B)
actors.description: Historical US airline fares and route economics by quarter, from the official BTS DB1B 10% ticket survey. Average and median fares, carrier market share and concentration (HHI), distance and estimated passengers by route, carrier or airport, with honest sample weighting. Not live booking prices.

sinceQuarter.description: First quarter of BTS DB1B data to include, as YYYY-Qn (e.g. "2025-Q1") or YYYY-n (e.g. "2025-1"), n being 1-4. Leave blank to default to the quarter before the latest published quarter. The DB1B Origin & Destination Survey begins 1993-Q1 and is published with a ~1-2 quarter lag; the run discovers the latest available quarter live and reports it on every row. An unusable value (a month form, slash date, bare year, or quarter 5) FAILS the run loudly — it is never silently ignored. Example: "2025-Q2".

untilQuarter.description: Last quarter of BTS DB1B data to include, as YYYY-Qn or YYYY-n. Leave blank to default to the latest published quarter. A window spanning more than 4 quarters is rejected (each quarter is a ~100 MB, ~7-million-row BTS download). A quarter BTS has not yet published is reported as missing — with allowPartial false (the default) the run fails loudly rather than quietly narrowing your window. Example: "2025-Q2".

origins.description: Optional. IATA origin airport codes, e.g. ["LAX","JFK"]. Leave empty for all origins. Markets are DIRECTIONAL in DB1B, so LAX-JFK and JFK-LAX are separate rows. An unfiltered, all-routes run over a full quarter aggregates tens of thousands of markets and is memory-heavy; a filter keeps it light. Example: ["LAX"].

dests.description: Optional. IATA destination airport codes, e.g. ["JFK","ORD"]. Leave empty for all destinations.

carriers.description: Optional. BTS ticketing-carrier codes to include, e.g. ["WN","AA","DL","UA","B6"]. Market share and fares are attributed to the TICKETING carrier (who sold the ticket); the operating carrier differs on ~27% of rows (codeshare/regional). Leave empty for all carriers (DB1B includes ~37 codes, incl. foreign carriers on US-endpoint itineraries and a "--" placeholder). A code matching no rows fails the run with the list of carriers actually present — never a silent empty dataset.

groupBy.description: How to roll markets up. "route" = one row per (directional origin-dest x quarter) across carriers; "carrier_route" = one row per (ticketing carrier x origin-dest x quarter); "origin_airport" = one row per (origin airport x quarter, all its outbound markets); "market" = one row per (origin city-market x dest city-market x quarter), which groups multi-airport metros (e.g. all NYC airports together). Carrier market-share/HHI fields are meaningful for route/origin_airport/market (which span carriers) and trivial for carrier_route. Omitted = "route". Example: "route".

minPassengers.description: Suppress groups with fewer than this many SAMPLE passengers in a quarter (noise control — a market with 2 sampled passengers gives a meaningless average fare). Remember DB1B is a 10% sample, so 10 sample passengers ~ 100 estimated. Suppressed-group count is disclosed on every emitted row as groups_suppressed_below_min_passengers. Set 0 to keep everything. Omitted = 10. Example: 10.

maxResults.description: Hard cap on emitted rows — each row is one billed result. Enforced by a single audited code path for every groupBy mode; when the cap bites, rows are dropped smallest-groups-first and every emitted row carries results_truncated=true. Omitted = 500. Example: 500.

allowPartial.description: If a requested quarter cannot be retrieved (not yet published by BTS, or the download failed), the run FAILS loudly by default so a partial window is never mistaken for a complete one. Set true to proceed with the quarters that did arrive — every row then reports quarters_missing and data_complete=false. Applied by default if omitted: false.

actors.title: California Data Broker Registry Monitor — CPPA Delete Act Delta
actors.description: California data broker registry API (CPPA / Delete Act): every registered data broker with 2026 disclosure flags (GenAI, foreign actor, minors, geolocation, biometric), DSAR metrics, first-registered year, new/lapsed/renamed/changed delta and is-this-company-registered verification.

mode.description: registry = the full CPPA registrant list (filterable) with 2026 disclosure flags, DSAR metrics and registration history. delta = only what changed since your last run: new, lapsed, renamed and changed registrants (the first run compares against CPPA's own 2025 export, so it is a real delta). verify = check names[] against the registry and get a three-valued is_registered per name. Example: "registry".

flags.description: Optional. Keep only registrants that filed Yes on EVERY listed flag. Keys: collects_minors, collects_account_logins, collects_government_ids, collects_citizenship_data, collects_union_membership, collects_sexual_orientation, collects_gender_identity, collects_biometric, collects_precise_geolocation, collects_reproductive_health, sold_to_foreign_actor, sold_to_federal_government, sold_to_state_governments, sold_to_law_enforcement, sold_to_genai_developer, regulated_fcra, regulated_glba, regulated_iippa, regulated_cmia, regulated_hipaa. An unknown key fails the run before any download.

nameQuery.description: Optional substring match on the registered name or DBA (case, punctuation and Inc/LLC suffixes ignored). Example: "transunion".

websiteQuery.description: Optional substring match on the filed website, e.g. "acxiom.com".

state.description: Optional. 2-letter code or full name ("CA" and "California" both match the same registrants — CPPA stores both spellings).

country.description: Optional exact match on the filed country, as CPPA publishes it in upper case (UNITED STATES, UNITED KINGDOM, CANADA...).

eventTypes.description: delta mode only. Optional subset of new, lapsed, renamed, changed. Empty = all four.

names.description: verify mode. One entry per company; you get one row per entry with is_registered true / false / null (null = fuzzy candidates exist, see evidence — review, do not treat as negative). Max 500. Example: ["Acxiom","LexisNexis","Oracle America"].

includeHistory.description: Also read CPPA's 2024 and 2025 exports and the legacy OAG 2020-2023 registry to fill first_registered_year / date, registration_years_seen and in_registry_* on every row. Three extra small downloads. Default on. Applied by default if omitted: true.

maxResults.description: Hard cap on rows emitted and billed (1-5000). The full registry is ~600 rows; every row carries matched_rows_total and results_truncated so a capped answer is never mistaken for the whole list. Example: 100.

actors.title: CalFire Fire Hazard Severity Zone (FHSZ) Screener — CA Parcels
actors.description: California Fire Hazard Severity Zone lookup against CalFire's currently adopted maps (SRA effective 2024-04-01, LRA dated 2025-03-24). Point-in-polygon per coordinate: hazard class, SRA/LRA/federal area, NHD disclosure flags, and a flag where the superseded 2007/2011 maps disagree.

assets.description: List of California properties/sites to screen for Fire Hazard Severity Zone status against CAL FIRE currently adopted maps (SRA dated 2023-09-29, effective 2024-04-01; LRA dated 2025-03-24). Each item is an object with numeric lat and lon (WGS84 decimal degrees) and an optional label. One billable result row is returned per asset, even when the site is clear. Example: [{"lat":37.8555,"lon":-122.21,"label":"Oakland Hills CA - SRA Very High"},{"lat":39.7596,"lon":-121.6219,"label":"Paradise CA - LRA Very High"},{"lat":39.328,"lon":-120.1833,"label":"Truckee CA - Very High only on the 2025 adopted map"},{"lat":38.582,"lon":-121.494,"label":"Downtown Sacramento CA - clear control"}].

checkNearby.description: When the exact coordinate is clear on every layer, also search for a mapped hazard zone within nearbyRadiusMiles (near-boundary flag). When off, nearby_zone_within_radius is reported as null (not checked) rather than false. Example: true.

nearbyRadiusMiles.description: Radius (miles) to search for a mapped FHSZ near a clear coordinate, when checkNearby is true. Clamped to 0.1-10 miles. Not used when the coordinate itself is already inside a mapped zone. Example: 0.5.

maxAssets.description: Safety cap on how many assets to screen in one run. Example: 500.

simulateOutage.description: Diagnostic only - leave as 'none' for real screening. 'control' forces the corroborating Sacramento negative-control query to fail, which must leave the run SUCCEEDING with drift_gate_status=verified_degraded, because that probe cross-checks a conclusion the load-bearing probes already establish. 'all' forces every drift query to fail, which must FAIL the run with zero rows and zero billing because the load-bearing probes can then confirm nothing. Example: "none".

actors.title: USFWS CBRS Coastal Barrier Screener - CBRA Flood Insurance Bar
actors.description: Batch-screen coordinates against the USFWS Coastal Barrier Resources System. Returns System Unit vs Otherwise Protected Area, the flood-insurance prohibition date FEMA actually applies, the official 20 ft boundary buffer zone, distance to the CBRS boundary, and the official unit map link.

assets.description: Points to check against the Coastal Barrier Resources System. Each item is an object with numeric lat and lon (WGS84 decimal degrees) and an optional label echoed into the output. One billable result row is produced per asset. Example: [{"lat":29.67,"lon":-85.35,"label":"Cape San Blas, FL (System Unit P30)"},{"lat":28.83752,"lon":-80.82921,"label":"Canaveral, FL (Otherwise Protected Area FL-07P)"},{"lat":29.751884,"lon":-85.304598,"label":"P30 boundary, FL (in unit and in the 20 ft buffer zone)"},{"lat":29.751884,"lon":-85.304567,"label":"3 m outside P30, FL (outside every unit - boundary-adjacent)"},{"lat":39.7392,"lon":-104.9…(truncated).

includeBoundaryPrecision.description: Query the official USFWS CBRS Buffer Zone layer (about 20 feet either side of a mapped boundary) and flag points that are boundary-adjacent. This does not change the in/out answer, which comes from the CBRS Units layer; it tells you that USFWS declines self-serve documentation that close to a line, so an official CBRS Property Determination letter is the way to document the point. Strongly recommended. Applied by default if omitted: true.

includeProhibitionDates.description: Query the CBRS Prohibitions layer for the flood insurance prohibition date and the System Unit designation date. FEMA uses the prohibition date to decide whether an existing structure inside the CBRS is still federally insurable, so this is the field that turns an in/out answer into an actionable one. Applied by default if omitted: true.

includeProximity.description: Measure the exact distance from each point to the nearest CBRS unit boundary and report the nearest unit within the search radius. Adds one query per asset. Applied by default if omitted: true.

includeOfficialMapLinks.description: Query the CBRS Map Panels layer for the panel number, the map effective date (the boundary vintage this result rests on) and a direct link to the official USFWS unit map so the answer can be verified against the legal map. Applied by default if omitted: true.

searchRadiusMeters.description: How far to look for nearby CBRS units when computing boundary distance. 1609 m is one mile. Larger radii return a nearest unit for more inland points at the cost of larger responses. Applied by default if omitted: 1609.

nearBoundaryMeters.description: Sets the informational near_boundary flag when a point is within this distance of a CBRS boundary. 76 m is about 250 feet, a typical lot depth. This is advisory only, at whatever threshold you set; the officially published band is the 20 ft CBRS Buffer Zone. Applied by default if omitted: 76.

maxAssets.description: Safety cap on how many assets to screen in one run. Extra assets beyond this limit are skipped. Applied by default if omitted: 500.

actors.title: CDC NNDSS Weekly Outbreak & Disease Anomaly Monitor
actors.description: Monitor CDC NNDSS weekly notifiable-disease cases. Computes spike ratio (current vs 52-week max), YoY cumulative change, and flags outbreak anomalies (new 52-week highs / spikes) per disease and reporting area. Keyless.

diseases.description: List of NNDSS disease/condition names to match (case-insensitive substring, e.g. "Measles" matches "Measles, Total" and "Measles, Imported"). Leave empty to include every notifiable condition. Multiple terms are OR-ed. Example: ["Measles"]. Applied by default if omitted: [].

areas.description: List of reporting areas to match (case-insensitive substring against the NNDSS 'states' column), e.g. ["Colorado", "New England", "U.S. Residents"]. Leave empty for all reporting areas. Multiple terms are OR-ed. Applied by default if omitted: [].

year.description: MMWR reporting year to filter on, e.g. "2026". Leave blank to include all available years (the dataset currently spans 2022 to the latest published week). Do not hard-code a stale year for recurring runs. Applied by default if omitted: "".

weekFrom.description: Optional lower bound MMWR week number (1-53). Rows before this week are excluded. Leave blank for no lower bound.

weekTo.description: Optional upper bound MMWR week number (1-53). Rows after this week are excluded. Leave blank for no upper bound.

minCases.description: Only keep rows whose current-week case count (m1) is at least this value. Rows with suppressed / null current counts are excluded when this is above 0. Default 0 keeps everything. Applied by default if omitted: 0.

anomalyThreshold.description: Flag a disease-week as an anomaly when spike_ratio (current-week cases / max of prior 52 weeks) is at or above this multiple. Default 2.0 (current at least double the 52-week peak). New 52-week highs are always flagged regardless. Example: "2.0".

onlyAnomalies.description: When true, only disease-week rows flagged as anomalies (new 52-week high, or spike_ratio at/above the threshold) are returned. Useful for outbreak-alert monitoring. Applied by default if omitted: false.

maxResults.description: Hard cap on the number of disease-week rows returned across all pages (protects run time and cost). Default 1000. Example: 140. Applied by default if omitted: 1000.

actors.title: CDFI Fund NMTC Low-Income Community Screener - IRA 48(e) Bonus
actors.description: Coordinate lookup for the IRA 48(e) low-income clean-energy bonus. Batch lat/lon against the DOE/NREL 48(e) Category 1 layer (IRC 45D(e) NMTC low-income communities). Returns a tract GEOID, Category 1 bonus flag, adder, Census tract coverage and a HUD QCT flag. MCP-ready.

assets.description: List of points to check against NMTC Low-Income Communities (LIC), read from the DOE/NREL Low-Income Communities Bonus Credit Program Category 1 eligibility layer. Each item is an object with numeric lat and lon (WGS84 decimal degrees) and an optional label echoed into the output. One billable result row is produced per asset, telling you whether the coordinate falls in a NMTC low-income community and therefore qualifies for the IRA 48(e) Category 1 clean-energy ITC bonus. A negative is published only when a separate Census census-tract coverage check confirms the point is inside a US tract; otherwise the flag is null (not checked), never false. Example: [{"lat":40.815,"lon":-73.904,"label":"South Bronx, NY (low-income community, also a LIHTC QCT)"},{"lat":35.6811,"lon":-109.0509,"label":"Window Rock, AZ (low-income community on the Navajo Nation)"},{"lat":34.073,"lon":-118.4,"label":"Beverly Hills, CA (genuine clear - not a low-income community)"}].

checkQct.description: When true (default), each asset is also checked against HUD's LIHTC Qualified Census Tract layer and the result carries an also_in_lihtc_qct flag (informational context; QCT is a LIHTC concept, not itself a 48(e) pathway). Set false to skip the extra lookup. Applied by default if omitted: true.

maxAssets.description: Safety cap on how many assets to screen in one run. Extra assets beyond this limit are skipped. Applied by default if omitted: 500.

checkTribal.description: When true (default), each asset is also checked against the U.S. Census Bureau TIGERweb Federal American Indian Reservations layer and the result carries on_federal_indian_reservation plus the reservation name. This is informational context for the separate IRC 48(e) Category 2 (Indian land) pathway - statutory Indian land under 25 U.S.C. 3501(2) is broader than federal reservations, so false does not rule Category 2 out. Set false to skip the extra lookup. Applied by default if omitted: true.

actors.title: Childcare Provider Leads — Daycare Contact Lists + Compliance
actors.description: Licensed childcare provider lead lists from official state licensing data in 9 states: TX, NY, CA, PA, MA, CT, WA, DE, VT. Phone, email and named contacts where published; filter by county, type, capacity, ages. Violation history where the state publishes it. Delta mode flags new programs.

state.description: REQUIRED. US state to pull licensed childcare providers from: TX, NY, CA, PA, MA, CT, WA, DE or VT. Name the state explicitly rather than relying on a default. To pull several states in one run, also fill "Additional states". Example: "TX".

states.description: Optional extra states to include in the same run, in addition to "State". maxResults is shared fairly across all requested states (a state that runs out of matches hands its unused share to the others). A state that cannot answer - source down, failed live check, or a filter it cannot apply - is skipped and disclosed on every row (run_states_failed / run_states_failed_reason); the run fails only if no requested state can answer.

county.description: Filter to one county (case-insensitive, e.g. "Harris", "Kings" or "Brooklyn", "Los Angeles", "Chester"). Leave empty for statewide. Connecticut and Massachusetts publish NO county field, so a county filter makes those states fail loudly rather than return an unfiltered statewide list. A county that does not exist returns 0 rows, which is a valid answer. Example: "Harris".

operationType.description: Exact operation type as the state names it (case-insensitive). Examples - TX: "Licensed Center", "Licensed Child-Care Home"; NY: "Day Care Center", "Group Family Day Care", "Family Day Care", "School Age Child Care" (or DCC/GFDC/FDC/SACC); PA: "Child Care Center", "Family Child Care Home", "Group Child Care Home"; CT: "Child Care Center", "Family Child Care Home"; DE: "Licensed Child Care Center"; VT: "CBCCPP", "Registered FCCH", "Licensed Provider"; WA: "CHILD CARE CENTER", "SCHOOL-AGE PROGRAM"; MA: "Center-based Care", "Family Child Care"; CA: "DAY CARE CENTER", "INFANT CENTER", "SCHOOL-AGE DC CENTER". Leave empty for all types. Example: "Licensed Center".

agesServed.description: Ages-served filter, e.g. "Infant", "Toddler", "Pre-Kindergarten", "School". TX and DE match the published ages text; NY and VT match programs with licensed capacity in that age group (Infant, Toddler, Preschool, School). PA, CT, WA, MA and CA publish no usable ages field, so this filter makes those states fail loudly rather than return unfiltered rows. Leave empty for any.

minCapacity.description: Only include operations whose published total licensed capacity is at or above this number (e.g. 50 targets larger centers). 0 = no minimum. Operations for which the state publishes NO capacity are KEPT and marked capacity_filter_applied="kept_unknown_capacity" rather than silently deleted - e.g. 141 of the 236 Texas Child Placing Agencies have no published capacity. Applied by default if omitted: 0.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of provider lead records to return (each record = one billed Result). Example: 100.

includeCompliance.description: Also attach each state's published compliance record. TX: 2-year non-compliance join (deficiency_count_2y, high_risk_flag ...) - the lifetime counts HHSC publishes on the roster row are emitted either way. CT: inspection + violation history. DE: non-compliance findings (last ~5 years). CA: CCLD facility page (status, contact, licensee, inspections, Type A/B citations, complaints). NY, PA, VT, WA and MA publish no compliance dataset: those rows read violations_status="not_published" with NULL counts, never 0. Example: true.

highRiskThreshold.description: Editorial heuristic: an operation is flagged high risk when its risk-weighted deficiency score (High 5, Medium High 3, Medium 2, Medium Low 1, Low 0.5) meets or exceeds this value. Applied to both the 2-year score (high_risk_flag) and the HHSC lifetime score (high_risk_flag_lifetime). Applied by default if omitted: 10.

mode.description: "roster" (default) returns the current filtered provider list. "new_operations" keeps a baseline of seen operation IDs in the NAMED key-value store "childcare-provider-leads-state", scoped to your state and filter combination (one baseline per state), and after the first seeding run emits only newly licensed operations. Every row carries delta_baseline_status so a seeding run is distinguishable from an incremental one. Applied by default if omitted: "roster".

activeOnly.description: Only include currently operating programs (TX operation_status = Y; NY not Suspended; CT ACTIVE; WA Active; MA not Expired). PA, DE, VT and CA publish current rosters only. Disable to include all statuses where the state publishes them. Applied by default if omitted: true.

actors.title: City Business License Leads — New Business Lead Feed API
actors.description: New business-license lead feed across Chicago, LA, SF, NYC and Seattle. Normalizes municipal open data into one schema with new-vs-renewal and active-vs-dead licence flags, owner mailing address, NAICS, phone where published, plus per-city coverage and freshness on every row.

cities.description: City slugs to pull business licenses from. Live and wired: chicago, los-angeles, san-francisco, new-york, seattle. Any other slug produces an explicit unknown_city / not_wired row rather than being silently dropped. Leave empty to query all live cities. Example: ["chicago"]. Applied by default if omitted: ["chicago","los-angeles","san-francisco","new-york","seattle"].

since.description: Only return licenses issued/started after this date, per each city's issue-date column. MUST be YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2025-01-15) - any other format is rejected and the run fails without billing, rather than silently returning every licence in the city as a new lead. Leave empty for the most recent records overall. Example: "2025-01-01".

name.description: Optional. Case-insensitive fragment matched against each city's business-name column (e.g. 'salon', 'LLC', a specific company).

licenseType.description: Optional. Case-insensitive fragment matched against the per-city license-type column (e.g. 'restaurant', 'pawnbroker', 'peddler'). Skipped for cities that do not expose a type column.

naics.description: Optional. NAICS code prefix to filter by industry (e.g. '72' = accommodation & food services, '5419' = professional services). Applied only in cities that expose NAICS (Los Angeles, Seattle).

onlyNewLicenses.description: On by default, so the feed matches what this Actor is sold as. Chicago publishes an application type and 76.1% of its 1.2M records are RENEW - existing businesses renewing, not new ones. With this on, Chicago is filtered server-side to ISSUE and C_LOC (a genuine new site) so you are not billed for renewals at all. Cities that publish no new-vs-renewal signal are NEVER dropped by this - their rows come back tagged record_kind "unknown". Turn it off to get every record. Example: true.

onlyActiveLicenses.description: On by default. Only 62.4% of the New York dataset is Active - the rest is Expired, Surrendered, Revoked, Voided, Suspended or explicitly Out of Business, and Chicago carries 78,619 cancelled plus 1,461 revoked licences. With this on those are excluded server-side. Cities that publish no status (LA, SF, Seattle) are NEVER dropped by this - their rows come back with is_active_license null. Turn it off to get every record. Example: true.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of rows for the WHOLE run, across all selected cities (each row is one billed result). Divided fairly between cities: a city with fewer matching licences than its share hands the rest to the others, and every city gets at least one row (a city that answers with nothing still emits one status row). Until build 1.1.7 this was a per-city cap, so an empty call across all 5 cities emitted 4,001 rows. Must be at least the number of cities selected. Example: 50. Applied by default if omitted: 1000.

socrataAppToken.description: Optional free Socrata app token to raise API rate limits for large pulls across many cities.

actors.title: Clinical Trials API - ClinicalTrials.gov, ISRCTN, EU CTIS
actors.description: Clinical trials API: search ClinicalTrials.gov, ISRCTN and the EU CTIS register in one call and get deduplicated trial records in a unified schema, with per-registry status on every row and optional patent linkage. Query by condition, drug, sponsor or status. Keyless, official registries.

query.description: A condition, drug, intervention, or sponsor to search across all registries (e.g. "melanoma", "semaglutide", "Pfizer"). Example: "melanoma".

sources.description: Which trial registries to include. ClinicalTrials.gov (US NIH), ISRCTN (UK/international) and EU CTIS are all keyless. The maxResults budget is shared FAIRLY across whichever you enable, so no single registry can fill the cap alone. Applied by default if omitted: ["clinicaltrials","isrctn","euctis"].

maxResults.description: Maximum number of deduplicated trial records to return. This is a true emit cap and therefore also your bill cap: one row written = one billable result. The budget is split max-min fairly across the registries you enabled, with trials found in 2+ distinct registries reserved off the top. Applied by default if omitted: 100.

onlyMultiRegistry.description: Return only trials found in more than one DISTINCT registry - the unique value of a meta-search. Applied before the maxResults cap. Corrected 2026-08-25: this previously also kept trials whose two merged records came from the same registry. Applied by default if omitted: false.

includePatents.description: Enrich each trial with related US patents matched on its interventions. Requires a free PatentsView API key; setting this to true without a key FAILS the run rather than silently returning zero patents on every row. Patents add columns, not rows, so they do not change what you are billed. Applied by default if omitted: false.

patentsViewApiKey.description: Free key from https://search.patentsview.org/ — only needed if 'Link related patents' is enabled.

actors.title: CMS Open Payments API — Physician Roll-up (Sunshine Act)
actors.description: CMS Open Payments (Sunshine Act) API: look up physician or manufacturer general payments by name, NPI or manufacturer, rolled up per physician × manufacturer — total USD, payment count, date range and payment-type mix. Pharma-compliance ready. Keyless, official CMS.

lastName.description: Covered-recipient (physician) last name to search for. Case-insensitive SUBSTRING match, so Smith also matches Goldsmith, Nesmith and Smithers. Combine with firstName to narrow. Leave blank to search by NPI, profile ID or manufacturer only. NOTE: this field deliberately has no schema default -- a default is injected server-side into every run, which silently AND-ed every NPI-only lookup with a last-name filter. Example: "Smith".

firstName.description: Covered-recipient (physician) first name. Case-insensitive substring match. Best used together with lastName.

npi.description: Exact 10-digit National Provider Identifier of the physician. The most precise way to look up one physician's payments.

profileId.description: Exact CMS Open Payments covered-recipient profile ID, if you already have it (an alternative precise physician key to NPI).

manufacturer.description: Name (or part of the name) of the drug/device manufacturer or GPO making the payment. Case-insensitive substring match. Use alone to profile a manufacturer, or with a physician filter to narrow to one relationship.

programYear.description: Reporting year to query, e.g. 2024. Leave blank to automatically use the most recent General Payments dataset published by CMS.

includeSpecialty.description: When on, look up each physician's specialty from the NPPES NPI registry when the payment record lacks one. Best-effort; never fails the run. Applied by default if omitted: false.

maxResults.description: Upper bound on raw payment rows fetched (in pages of 500) before aggregating. NOTE: CMS paginates via SQL OFFSET, which slows sharply past ~2000 rows; a time budget stops very deep pulls and returns partial results. Narrow the filter (add firstName/NPI/manufacturer) for complete deep results. Example: 500. Applied by default if omitted: 2000.

actors.title: Medicare Part D Drug Spending Delta & Top Movers API (CMS)
actors.description: Year-over-year Medicare Part D drug spending deltas and top movers from the keyless CMS API. Get spend change %, per-claim and per-beneficiary cost change, claims and beneficiary deltas, and CAGR per drug. Filter by drug, manufacturer, min spend or min change. No API key.

mode.description: "top_movers" ranks drugs by the size of their year-over-year spending change (best for finding price/utilization movers). "search" returns every drug matching your filters, still sorted by the chosen field. Example: "top_movers".

drugName.description: Case-insensitive substring match against the brand name and generic name (e.g. "Ozempic", "Semaglutide", "insulin"). Leave empty to include all drugs.

manufacturer.description: Case-insensitive substring match against the manufacturer name (e.g. "Novo Nordisk", "Pfizer"). Supplying this automatically includes the per-manufacturer rows (not just the drug's "Overall" summary).

minSpendLatest.description: Only include drugs whose most recent year of total Medicare Part D spending is at least this many US dollars. Use it to focus on high-impact drugs and filter out long-tail noise. Example: 100000000. Applied by default if omitted: 0.

minAbsChangePct.description: Only include drugs whose absolute year-over-year total-spending change is at least this percent (e.g. 25 keeps drugs that rose or fell by 25%+). 0 disables the filter. Applied by default if omitted: 0.

sortBy.description: Metric used to rank results. NOTE: a drug in its FIRST Part D year has no percentage change (the base does not exist), so it cannot appear on a percentage ranking. Sort by "spending_change_abs_incl_new_entrants" to rank launches alongside continuing drugs. Rows with no value for the chosen key always sort LAST, in both directions. Example: "spending_change_pct".

sortDirection.description: "desc" surfaces the biggest increases (or highest values) first; "asc" surfaces the biggest decreases (or lowest values) first. Example: "desc".

requireLatestYear.description: When true (recommended), only include drugs whose most recent data year equals the dataset's newest year, so every result is the same fresh year-over-year comparison and discontinued drugs are excluded. Turn off to include drugs that stopped reporting in earlier years. Example: true.

includeManufacturerBreakdown.description: When false (default), returns one "Overall" row per drug. When true, also returns a row per manufacturer for each drug (useful for multi-source generics). Applied by default if omitted: false.

topN.description: In "top_movers" mode, cap the output to the top N ranked drugs after filtering and sorting. Example: 100.

maxResults.description: Hard cap on the number of records written to the dataset (billed as results). Applied by default if omitted: 1000.

newEntrantsOnly.description: Emit only drugs in their first published Medicare Part D year. 197 of 3,625 drugs (5.4%) were new entrants in the 2024 edition. Applied by default if omitted: false.

requireYearOverYear.description: Drop drugs whose latest and prior published years are more than one year apart, so every spending_change_pct in the result is a genuine year-over-year figure. 23 live rows span more than one year. Applied by default if omitted: false.

actors.title: Sanctions Screening List Change Monitor — CSL / OFAC Delta API
actors.description: Sanctions screening list change monitor. Diffs the US Trade.gov Consolidated Screening List (OFAC SDN/Non-SDN, BIS Entity/Denied/Unverified/MEU, State DDTC/ISN) against the last run and emits added/removed/modified entries with field-level changes. Keyless. Monitoring tool, not compliance advice.

mode.description: 'delta' returns only entries ADDED, REMOVED or MODIFIED since this actor's previous run (the change feed, computed against a named cross-run key-value store). 'full' returns the complete current list as a snapshot. On the FIRST delta run there is no baseline, so every current entry is reported with change_type 'added' and is_baseline_row=true - read delta_comparable before treating any row as a new designation. Example: "full". Applied by default if omitted: "delta".

name.description: Case-insensitive substring match against the primary name AND all aliases (alt_names). Use to watch a specific person, company or vessel. Empty = all entries. In delta mode the filter is applied to the CHANGES, after the full-list diff, so filtering can never fabricate 'removed' rows.

source.description: Keep only entries whose source list or agency group matches this text. Matches the full list name or the coarse group, e.g. 'OFAC', 'Treasury', 'Entity List', 'BIS', 'Denied Persons', 'State', 'ITAR'. Empty = all lists.

program.description: Keep only entries tagged with a sanctions/control program containing this text, e.g. 'IRAN', 'RUSSIA', 'CMIC', 'SDGT', 'CAATSA'. Empty = all programs.

country.description: Keep only entries whose nationality, citizenship, place of birth, or address mentions this text, e.g. 'China', 'CN', 'Russia', 'Iran'. Empty = all countries.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of change (or snapshot) records to emit after filtering. One record = one billable result. Example: 100. Applied by default if omitted: 1000.

monitor.description: When true, save the current full list to the actor's key-value store so the NEXT run can compute a delta against it. Keep true for scheduled change-monitoring. Set false for a one-off read that must not overwrite the stored baseline. Applied by default if omitted: true.

actors.title: Distressed Property Leads - NYC, Detroit, Philly & Chicago
actors.description: Motivated-seller leads for New York City, Detroit, Philadelphia and Chicago. Stacks open code violations, blight tickets, tax liens, evictions, vacant-building complaints and scofflaw listings per property, scores distress, and attaches the owner name and mailing address. Keyless government data.

metros.description: Which metro lead pipelines to run. Defaults to New York City only, which is exactly what this actor did before multi-metro support, so saved tasks and API callers that omit this field are unaffected. Detroit and Philadelphia publish the owner name and mailing address on the violation record itself. Chicago publishes neither and is matched to the Cook County assessor roll on an exact address, so its owner-match rate is lower and is reported on every row. Add metros one at a time: each one is a separate full-city scan and you are billed per result. Example: ["nyc"].

enumTitles: New York City (violations + tax liens + evictions)

borough.description: NYC borough to scan. Accepts a name (MANHATTAN, BRONX, BROOKLYN, QUEENS, STATEN ISLAND) or a borough code 1-5. One borough per run keeps runs fast and cheap. Applies only when "nyc" is one of the selected metros; it is ignored by Detroit, Philadelphia and Chicago, which are scanned city-wide. Example: "BRONX".

minSignals.description: Only emit parcels showing at least this many DIFFERENT distress signal types (open violations, tax-lien-sale notice, executed evictions). 2 = solid motivated-seller leads; 3 = only the most distressed parcels; 1 = everything with any signal. Example: 2.

lookbackMonths.description: How many months of history to count, anchored to each dataset's own most-recent record date (not today) so a lagging source like the lien-sale list still yields its latest cycle. Applies to violation issue dates, lien-sale list months, and eviction execution dates. Example: 12.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of ranked parcel leads to emit (highest distress score first). You are billed per result, so this caps your spend. Example: 100.

actors.title: DoD Military Installation & FIRRMA Site Proximity Screener
actors.description: Screen any US coordinate against DoD MIRTA installation boundaries: on-installation verdict, reporting component, joint-base status, and the published FIRRMA site flag with measured distance for CFIUS Part 802 diligence.

assets.description: One entry per coordinate to screen. Each needs lat and lon in WGS84 decimal degrees, an optional label, and an optional radiusMiles that overrides the run-level radius. Example: [{"lat":39.7017,"lon":-104.7514,"label":"Aurora CO parcel","radiusMiles":25}]. Required - a run with no assets fails loudly and bills nothing. Example: [{"lat":39.7017,"lon":-104.7514,"label":"Aurora CO parcel (adjacent to Buckley SFB)","radiusMiles":25},{"lat":36.8508,"lon":-76.2859,"label":"Norfolk VA waterfront site","radiusMiles":15},{"lat":32.7157,"lon":-117.1611,"label":"San Diego CA industrial parcel","radiusMiles":15},{"lat":41.5,"lon":-100,"label":"Rural Nebraska control parcel","radiusMiles":25}].

radiusMiles.description: How far from each coordinate to look for DoD installations. Applies to any asset that does not set its own radiusMiles. Defaults to 25 when omitted; maximum 250. Deliberately has no schema default, because an Apify input-schema default is injected server-side into every run and a default on a query predicate silently narrows queries the caller never wrote. Example: 25.

firrmaScanMiles.description: Separate, usually wider radius used only to find sites DoD flags with ISFIRRMASITE, so the CFIUS-adjacent proximity bands can be reported honestly. Defaults to 100 when omitted; maximum 250. Any reported band wider than this radius is null (not checked), never false. Example: 100.

includeInstallationDetail.description: When true (the default) the run emits an asset_summary row per site plus an installation row for each DoD installation found within the radius. Set false for summary rows only. Applied by default if omitted: true.

activeOnly.description: When true, installation detail rows are limited to sites whose published operational status is Active or is not decodable. Sites with an unmapped status code are KEPT, because an undefined code is not evidence a site is inactive. Summary counts are unaffected. Applied by default if omitted: false.

maxInstallationsPerAsset.description: Caps how many installation detail rows are emitted per screened coordinate, nearest first. Defaults to 25 when omitted. Example: 25.

maxAssets.description: Safety cap on how many coordinates a single run will screen. Defaults to 25 when omitted; maximum 100. Example: 25.

skipDriftChecks.description: Diagnostic only. The live drift gate verifies feature counts, the published coded-value vocabularies, a positive canary (Buckley Space Force Base) and a negative control before any billable row is produced. Disabling it removes the protection against a silently changed upstream. Applied by default if omitted: false.

simulateOutage.description: Diagnostic seam that forces one or all upstream layers to fail, so the null-versus-false contract and the billing gate can be re-proved on demand instead of only during a real outage. Leave as none for normal use. Applied by default if omitted: "none".

actors.title: DOL Enforcement Rollup — Employer Wage-Theft Violator API
actors.description: Roll up US Department of Labor enforcement actions by employer. Aggregates WHD wage-theft cases (back wages, penalties, employees affected) with optional EBSA/ERISA into per-employer summaries and repeat-violator flags.

apiKey.description: Your free U.S. Department of Labor Open Data API key. Register at https://dataportal.dol.gov/registration (instant, free) and paste it here, or set the DOL_API_KEY environment variable. Required -- the DOL data endpoint rejects unauthenticated requests, and this actor fails loudly rather than returning an empty dataset that would read as "no enforcement history".

mode.description: "rollup" returns one aggregated row per employer (total back wages, total cases, employees affected, finding date range, agency list, repeat_violator flag). "cases" returns one normalized row per individual enforcement case. Applied by default if omitted: "rollup".

sources.description: Which DOL agencies to pull. Empty = WHD only (Wage and Hour Division — the shippable default). Add EBSA to include ERISA Form 5500 penalty cases (OCATS). OFCCP is scaffolded but not yet enabled. Applied by default if omitted: [].

employer.description: Optional. Case-insensitive substring matched against the employer trade name and legal name (e.g. "walmart", "tyson foods"). Leave blank to return all employers. Names made entirely of corporate stop-words ("The Group") fall back to a raw substring match.

state.description: Optional. Filter to employers in a single US state by its 2-letter postal code (e.g. "CA", "TX", "NY"). Example: "CA".

naics.description: Optional. Filter by industry NAICS code prefix (e.g. "722" for food service, "23" for construction). Matches codes that start with this value.

sinceDate.description: Optional. Only include cases whose findings end date is after this date. MUST be YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2023-01-01) - any other format FAILS the run without billing, rather than being guessed at. The value is compared against DOL's own ISO date column and is also sent to DOL as a server-side 'gt' filter, so a bad format does not error upstream - it silently returns the WHOLE case set or NONE of it, and neither is visible in the output. Measured on this actor: 01/15/2023 returned 3 of 3 cases labelled as filtered; Jan 2023 returned 0 of 3, a confident 'no enforcement cases'. Slash forms are rejected on purpose: 05/06/2025 is ambiguous between US (May 6) and EU (June 5) order. 2023-1-1 is accepted and zero-padded. Leave blank for no date filter. Example: "2023-01-01".

repeatThreshold.description: In rollup mode, an employer is flagged repeat_violator when its total case count is greater than this value (default 1 = more than one case). Any case carrying a WHD repeat/willful flag also sets it true. If the fetch was capped or a source failed, a NEGATIVE verdict is returned as null -- see repeat_violator_basis. Applied by default if omitted: 1.

maxResults.description: Cap on the number of raw enforcement cases fetched PER source before rollup. When a source hits this cap the result is a slice, not a complete history: every row is marked result_truncated=true, total_cases becomes a floor rather than a count, and a NEGATIVE repeat_violator verdict is returned as null instead of false. Raise it for a full pull. Example: 500. Applied by default if omitted: 2000.

actors.title: Drug Shortage API — Delta Monitor & FDA Shortage Tracker
actors.description: Drug shortage API on the official openFDA feed: normalized shortage records, delta monitor mode that emits only NEW or status-CHANGED shortages (new/resolved/reappeared), and therapeutic-class + dosage-form rollups of current shortages. Keyless.

status.description: Which FDA shortage status to return. LIVE 2026-08-01 the feed holds Current 1,180 | To Be Discontinued 432 | Resolved 24. 'To Be Discontinued' is a planned permanent product discontinuation, not a supply shortage - it lives in the same FDA feed and is selectable here from v1.1 onward. Applied server-side as an openFDA search filter. Example: "Current".

therapeuticCategory.description: Optional therapeutic-class filter applied server-side (openFDA therapeutic_category), e.g. 'Oncology' (135 records live), 'Psychiatry' (281), 'Analgesia/Addiction' (185), 'Cardiovascular' (161). Leave empty for all categories.

sinceDate.description: Only return shortages whose update date (or initial posting date when no update) is on or after this date. Accepted forms: 2025-01-15 (ISO, preferred), 2025-01, 2025, or 01/15/2025 (US month/day/year). Anything else FAILS the run rather than being guessed at — this value is compared against ISO dates, so an unusable format would silently return either the entire feed or nothing at all, with no error. Leave blank for no lower bound. Example: "2025-01-15".

maxResults.description: Maximum number of records to fetch and normalize. The whole feed is ~1,636 records and openFDA pages at 1,000 per request, so 3,000 covers everything with headroom. Setting this BELOW the number of matching records truncates the fetch - every row will then carry feed_complete=false, the rollup counts will be computed over the subset, and delta mode will refuse to run rather than invent events for records it never read. Example: 3000.

monitor.description: When scheduled, emit only records that are NEW or whose status CHANGED since the previous run, each tagged change_type (new, resolved, reappeared, discontinuing, discontinuation_cancelled, delisted, updated). Unchanged records are skipped. State lives in a NAMED key-value store, keyed to this query scope, so a scheduled run genuinely compares against the last run. Requires a complete fetch: if maxResults truncates the feed, the run fails rather than fabricating events. Applied by default if omitted: false.

includeRollup.description: Also emit summary rows (record_type='rollup') per therapeutic_category and per dosage_form, counting current shortages, planned discontinuations, resolved records and the total. Applied by default if omitted: false.

skipDriftAssertions.description: Diagnostic escape hatch. By default the Actor runs 10 live checks against openFDA before emitting anything billable (feed size in band, the status and update_type vocabularies still closed, a known-populated therapeutic category returning rows, a known-nonexistent one returning none, required fields present, feed freshness, and that skip= genuinely advances the page) and fails the run rather than reporting drug-supply status from a drifted source. Turn this on only if you believe a check is a false positive. Applied by default if omitted: false.

actors.title: Electricity Rates & Grid Mix by State — EIA Site Economics
actors.description: Electricity cost screening by state from the EIA v2 API: industrial, commercial and residential retail rates with YoY change and a live US benchmark, plus operating capacity by fuel, balancing authority, storage split and planned retirements. For data-center and industrial siting.

apiKey.description: Free EIA v2 API key. Register in about a minute at https://www.eia.gov/opendata/register.php (no cost, no card). Supplying your own key gives you your own rate limit; leave it blank to use the Actor default key, which is shared across all users. If no key is available at all the run FAILS loudly with the registration URL and bills nothing - it does not return a green empty dataset. You may also set an EIA_API_KEY environment variable on the Actor.

states.description: Two-letter US state ids to build an electricity-economics profile for (e.g. "CO", "TX"). One billable state_profile row per state. "US" is also accepted for the national aggregate. An id EIA does not publish is flagged state_id_recognized=false rather than returned as a state with zero capacity. Example: ["CO","TX"].

months.description: How many months of retail-rate history to fetch per state. Used to find the latest month and compute the same-month year-over-year price change, so 13 is the minimum for one full YoY comparison. Does not affect the capacity rollup, which always uses the newest published month. Applied by default if omitted: 24.

includePlantDetail.description: When true, also emit one billable row per GENERATOR (row_type "plant") with plant name and id, operator, balancing authority, fuel, technology, prime mover, nameplate and net summer/winter capacity, in-service date, planned retirement date, county and lat/lon - capped by "Max plant rows". When false (default) only the one state_profile summary row per state is returned. Applied by default if omitted: false.

maxPlantRows.description: Safety cap on the number of per-generator rows emitted per state when "Include per-plant capacity rows" is true. Each row is billable. Ignored when that option is false. Applied by default if omitted: 200.

actors.title: BLM Section 368 Energy Corridor Screener - Federal ROW Siting
actors.description: Screens coordinates against BLM Section 368 West-wide Energy Corridors using BLM current designations plus the Argonne mirror. Returns corridor name, width, permitted use, whether a later plan amendment deleted it, distance to the nearest corridor and a ROW streamlining signal.

assets.description: Sites to screen for point-in-polygon / proximity to a designated Section 368 West-wide Energy Corridor. Each entry is an object { "lat": number, "lon": number, "label": "optional name", "radiusMiles": optional number }. Also accepts "lat,lon" strings or [lat, lon] arrays. The optional per-asset "radiusMiles" overrides the global search radius. One dataset row (one billed result) is produced per asset; a bad entry yields an ERROR row and the run continues. Example: [{"lat":34.57155,"lon":-115.54038,"label":"Mojave, CA - inside corridor 27-41 (multi-modal, BLM)","radiusMiles":10},{"lat":43.52738,"lon":-116.96533,"label":"SW Idaho - corridor 11-228, in BLM current data but not the 2020 mirror","radiusMiles":10},{"lat":41.673613,"lon":-107.700677,"label":"S. Wyoming - corridor 78-138 realigned since the 2020 mirror","radiusMiles":10},{"lat":39.7392,"lon":-104.…(truncated).

radiusMiles.description: Default radius, in miles, around each asset to search for a designated Section 368 Energy Corridor (1-50; internally clamped down to 0.25 if a smaller per-asset value is supplied). Designated corridors are sparse and narrow, so a wider default than typical proximity screens is used. Overridden by a per-asset "radiusMiles". Default 10. Example: 10.

maxAssets.description: Maximum number of assets processed in one run (1-2000). One result row is emitted (and billed) per asset. Default 500. Example: 500.

actors.title: EPA AirToxScreen Cancer Risk Screener - Census Tract Air Toxics
actors.description: EPA AirToxScreen 2019 census-tract cancer-risk API: total risk per million, top contributing pollutants, point/on-road/non-road/non-point source attribution, non-cancer hazard index, and a live national percentile. For Phase I due diligence and environmental-justice screening.

assets.description: List of points to screen against EPA AirToxScreen 2019 census-tract air-toxics cancer risk. Each item needs numeric lat/lon and an optional label. Example: [{"lat":29.7355,"lon":-95.24,"label":"Houston Ship Channel / Manchester, TX"},{"lat":34.0339,"lon":-118.2076,"label":"Boyle Heights, Los Angeles, CA"},{"lat":39.7392,"lon":-104.9903,"label":"Denver, CO"},{"lat":39.3,"lon":-101,"label":"Rural Thomas County, KS"}].

includeAllPollutants.description: When true, also emit ambient_concentrations_ug_m3 (all 177 EPA-modeled ambient air-toxics concentrations) and cancer_risk_by_pollutant_full (all 72 named cancer-risk pollutants, not just the top ranked ones) on every matched row. Off by default to keep the row curated rather than a 318-field dump. Applied by default if omitted: false.

topPollutantsCount.description: How many top-contributing cancer-risk pollutants to rank and return per matched tract (by CR_* value, descending). Maximum 72 (the full named-pollutant list). Applied by default if omitted: 10.

maxAssets.description: Safety cap on how many assets one run will screen, regardless of how many are supplied in "assets". Applied by default if omitted: 200.

actors.title: Phase I ESA & Environmental Due Diligence: EPA Database Search
actors.description: Environmental due diligence by address: an environmental database report over EPA Superfund/NPL, RCRA CORRACTS/TSD/generators, TRI, UST, LUST, Brownfields, NPDES, AIR, TSCA and RMP, scored at ASTM E1527-21 search distances, plus on-site Superfund and AUL boundary checks. No API key.

mode.description: "assets" (default) runs a multi-database Phase I ESA-style regulatory-records screen on your addresses/coordinates — one billable row per nearby EPA-listed site (across Superfund, RCRA, TRI, UST, LUST and Brownfields). "inventory" instead dumps the raw list of EPA SEMS/Superfund sites for the states you pick — one billable row per site. Example: "assets".

assets.description: Locations to screen against EPA contaminated-site databases. Each item is EITHER {"address": "...", "label": "..."} (geocoded via the free Census geocoder) OR {"lat": <number>, "lon": <number>, "label": "...", "state": "<2-letter, OPTIONAL>"}. The "state" hint is no longer required with lat/lon — Superfund is now also screened spatially against the EPA FRS SEMS point layers, which need no state. Supplying "state" additionally pulls that state's full Envirofacts SEMS roster for wider non-NPL coverage. One dataset row (one billable check) is produced per site hit found within the radius; assets with no hits return a single "clear" row. If EVERY asset fails input validation the run FAILS and nothing is billed. Example: [{"lat":39.8037,"lon":-104.9986,"state":"CO","label":"Denver industrial parcel (lat/lon input)"},{"address":"5980 Lipan St, Denver, CO 80221","label":"Denver industrial parcel (address input)"}].

radiusMiles.description: Distance from each asset within which EPA-listed sites are counted and reported across all selected programs. Accepts fractional miles (0.1-50) so you can screen at the ASTM E1527-21 standard search distances directly: 1.0 mi (NPL / RCRA CORRACTS), 0.5 mi (SEMS-CERCLIS, RCRA TSD, LUST, Brownfields), 0.25 mi (registered UST, RCRA generators). Default 1 mile covers the widest ASTM distance. Example: 1.

programs.description: Which EPA program databases to include. The six defaults: SUPERFUND (NPL/SEMS), RCRA (hazardous-waste handlers, now classified into CORRACTS / TSD / generator), TRI (Toxics Release Inventory), UST (underground storage tanks), LUST (leaking USTs), BROWNFIELD (ACRES/FRS). Four additional opt-in programs come from the SAME EPA ECHO response at no extra upstream call: NPDES (Clean Water Act discharge permits), AIR (Clean Air Act permitted sources), TSCA (incl. PCB handlers), RMP (Risk Management Plan chemical-accident facilities). Leave EMPTY to screen the original six only — that keeps row counts and cost identical to previous versions.
